title: Deduplicate events before they reach the warehouse
subtitle: The loader keys rows by event id and the warehouse merges instead of appending

nodes.label: etl/load.py
nodes.diff:
@@ -8,4 +8,5 @@ def batch(rows):
     out = []
-    for r in rows:
+    seen = set()
+    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r.ts):
         out.append(r.to_row())
@@ -21,3 +22,4 @@ def flush(out):
-    db.execute("COPY events FROM STDIN", out)
+    db.execute("COPY staging FROM STDIN", out)
+    db.execute(open("merge.sql").read())
     log.info("flushed %d", len(out))

nodes.label: etl/merge.sql

steps.caption: Before: every batch was appended, duplicates and all
Hunk 1: batches are sorted by timestamp
…so the newest copy of an event wins
Hunk 2: COPY into a staging table, then run merge.sql
merge.sql inserts only unseen event ids
The warehouse sees each event once
